prologue.title: The Village of Twiggle
prologue.narrator: Sometimes days move so fast that people forget to live them.
prologue.text:
You arrive in the village of Twiggle with your friend Aikito.

Aikito is a curious little dog who loves to play, chase leaves and cars, and ask far too many questions.

But today, something feels strange.

The villagers are running everywhere.

Everyone keeps saying:

“Quick!”
“No time!”
“Later!”

Even the children have stopped playing.

Far away, a huge ticking sound echoes from the hill.

Aikito sniffs the air and frowns with his tiny eyebrows.

*“It smells strange... like when you're late for something you never planned.”*

choices.text: Follow the sound with Aikito
Stay and play with the children

jeu.title: Five More Minutes
jeu.narrator: Sometimes playing matters more than rushing.
jeu.text:
You suggest a game of ball.

At first, nobody dares.

Then Aikito catches the ball with his head and falls into a puddle.

Everyone bursts out laughing.

Even the grown-ups stop for a few seconds.

The ticking seems to slow down a little.

A little girl with red hair comes up to you.

*“What kind of dog is that? Does he always do stuff like that?”*

Aikito shakes his head and sends water everywhere. Everyone laughs even harder.

choices.text: Play a little longer with the girl
Go up the hill with Aikito

nouvelle_amie.title: Leonie
nouvelle_amie.narrator: A new friendship often begins with laughter.
nouvelle_amie.text:
Her name is Leonie. She has lived in Twiggle all her life.

*“We used to play here all the time,”* she says. *“And then the clock started going too fast. Now everyone is in a hurry and nobody has time for anything.”*

Aikito sits down in front of her and tilts his head.

*“Even the butterflies go faster,”* he says gravely. *“I tried to catch one this morning. It was already gone before I'd finished getting up.”*

Leonie laughs.

*“Your dog talks?”*

*“Only when it's important,”* you reply.

choices.text: Ask Leonie what is on the hill
Go up the hill all together

leonie_raconte.title: What Leonie Knows
leonie_raconte.narrator: Les enfants remarquent souvent des choses que les adultes ont arrêté de voir.
leonie_raconte.text:
Leonie sits down on a bench. She speaks softly.

*“The clock appeared three weeks ago. At first you could barely hear it. Then people started checking the time all the time. Then running. Then forgetting to eat, to laugh, to look at the sky.”*

She looks down at her shoes.

*“My dad stopped telling me bedtime stories. He says he doesn't have time anymore. But in the evening... the time is there. He just can't see it anymore.”*

Aikito rests his head on Leonie's knees.

*“Your dad needs someone to give him his time back,”* he says.

choices.text: Go up the hill with Leonie and Aikito

chemin_colline.title: The Hill Path
chemin_colline.location: PATH — BETWEEN THE VILLAGE AND THE HILL
chemin_colline.narrator: Le chemin vers la colline est plein de choses à regarder, si on prend le temps.
chemin_colline.text:
The path climbs gently.

Aikito stops every two minutes to sniff something.

*“A snail came this way this morning,”* he says. *“It was going the wrong way. I didn't tell it. I didn't want to hurt its feelings.”*

You look down at the village. People are still running. One man is in such a hurry that he forgets his hat. He comes back for his hat and forgets his basket. He comes back for his basket and...

*“They forget things because they go too fast,”* says Aikito. *“If you go too fast, you lose little bits of yourself along the way.”*

choices.text: Continue toward the summit
Stop and watch a cloud with Aikito

chemin_colline_amis.title: The Path for Three
chemin_colline_amis.location: PATH — BETWEEN THE VILLAGE AND THE HILL
chemin_colline_amis.narrator: Les chemins sont plus beaux à plusieurs.
chemin_colline_amis.text:
Leonie walks beside you. Aikito runs ahead, comes back, runs off again.

He picks up a leaf and solemnly places it at Leonie's feet.

*“This is for you,”* he says. *“It fell from the tree at exactly the right moment.”*

Leonie laughs and takes the leaf.

*“How does he know it was the right moment?”*

*“I don't know,”* you say. *“Aikito says lots of things that sound like they make no sense and always turn out to make sense.”*

Aikito nods with great dignity.

choices.text: Continue toward the summit

nuage.title: The Dog-Shaped Cloud
nuage.narrator: Regarder les nuages est une des choses les plus importantes qu'on puisse faire.
nuage.text:
You both lie down in the grass.

Aikito points his nose at the sky.

*“That one looks like a dog chasing a ball,”* he says.

You look. He's right.

*“And that one looks like a hat that lost its owner,”* you add.

You stay there for a while. The ticking of the clock is still there, but from far away it almost sounds like music.

*“I wonder if the clock is sad,”* says Aikito. *“Going so fast all the time. I would be sad.”*

You hadn't thought of it that way.

choices.text: Go see the clock up close

colline.title: The Giant Clock
colline.narrator: Certaines horloges donnent l'heure. D'autres décident du rythme du monde.
colline.text:
You and Aikito reach the top of the hill.

A huge clock is turning much too fast.

With every tick:
- the grown-ups run faster,
- the children put away their toys,
- the sun seems to race across the sky.

Aikito looks at you.

*“Maybe the villagers forgot to take their time…”*

Up close, the clock is covered in little carvings — children playing, grown-ups laughing, families eating together.

*“It used to be beautiful,”* Aikito says softly. *“I can feel it.”*

choices.text: Sit calmly with Aikito
Try to stop the clock
Look at the carvings more closely

gravures_horloge.title: What the Clock Remembers
gravures_horloge.location: MINUTE HILL — FOOT OF THE CLOCK
gravures_horloge.narrator: Les objets anciens gardent la mémoire de ce qu'ils ont vu.
gravures_horloge.text:
You step closer and put your fingers on the carvings.

Children running through meadows. An old man fishing. A mom reading a story. A dad looking at the stars with his daughter.

*“It remembers,”* says Aikito. *“The clock remembers when time was gentle.”*

You look at the hands spinning at full speed. They almost seem... out of breath.

*“I think someone told it to go faster one day,”* says Aikito. *“And it obeyed. But nobody ever told it to stop.”*

That gives you an idea.

choices.text: Speak softly to the clock
Sit down and set an example

parler_horloge.title: A Conversation with Time
parler_horloge.narrator: On peut parler à n'importe quoi, si on y met du cœur.
parler_horloge.text:
You put your hand on the warm wood of the clock.

*“You can slow down,”* you say softly. *“Nobody needs to go this fast. The people down there have forgotten to look at the sky. They've forgotten to laugh. They need time.”*

Aikito adds, very seriously:

*“And I need time to catch butterflies.”*

The clock doesn't answer. But something changes — the ticking is a tiny bit softer.

Not enough yet. But a little.

choices.text: Sit with Aikito and keep being calm

sasseoir.title: Sitting Down
sasseoir.narrator: Parfois la chose la plus courageuse est de ne pas se presser.
sasseoir.text:
You both sit down in the grass, facing the clock.

Aikito yawns and rests his head on your knees.

The hands keep spinning fast.

But you don't move.

A bird lands near you. Then another. Even the birds seem curious about two creatures who refuse to hurry.

*“I think the clock is watching us,”* Aikito whispers.

You look at the hands. Maybe he's right.

They seem... to hesitate.

choices.text: Stay a little longer and do nothing

arreter_horloge.title: Aikito's Plan
arreter_horloge.narrator: Les grands projets commencent souvent par des petites idées.
arreter_horloge.text:
You walk up to the clock. It is huge — its gears turn with a rumble.

Aikito thinks hard, paws crossed.

*“I could bite a gear,”* he suggests.

*“No.”*

*“I could sit on it.”*

*“No.”*

*“We could sing really loudly until it stops out of embarrassment?”*

You look at Aikito. He is completely serious.

*“I have a better idea,”* you say.

choices.text: Share your idea with Aikito

idee_cle.title: The Key of Time
idee_cle.narrator: La bonne idée arrive toujours au bon moment.
idee_cle.text:
*“What if we didn't try to stop it? What if we just showed it... what calm looks like?”*

Aikito tilts his head.

*“Like an example?”*

*“Like an example.”*

You both sit down in the grass, facing the huge clock.

Aikito pulls a ball out of nowhere and bounces it gently. Once. Twice. Slowly.

You look at the sky.

The hands hesitate.

choices.text: Keep being calm together

fin_douce.title: Time to Play
fin_douce.narrator: Some things need time to become beautiful.
fin_douce.text:
You and Aikito watch the sun go down.

The clock slows down gently.

In the village, the children start playing again.

The grown-ups finally stop rushing around.

Aikito wags his tail, then says softly:

*"Grown-ups sometimes forget to play.*
*I don't want to forget."*

You look down at Twiggle — laughter floats up to you, light as soap bubbles.

The clock keeps ticking. But now it keeps the right pace. Not too fast. Not too slow.

Just... the time it takes.

fin_amis.title: Evening in Twiggle
fin_amis.narrator: The best days are the ones nobody planned.
fin_amis.text:
The sun sets over Twiggle.

The clock has slowed down. The laughter has come back.

Leonie runs to her dad, who is waiting for her on the doorstep.

He crouches down, opens his arms, and this time... he doesn't look at the time.

Aikito nudges you with his nose.

*“See? He found his time again.”*

In the sky, the first stars appear.

*“There's a star for every moment we take the time to live,”* says Aikito.

*“Is that true?”*

*“I don't know. But it's a nice thing to believe.”*
